A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lychee-FD research and provide complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices 7–11. Text and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Lychee-FD benchmark results, component and layer ablations, gradient analyses, and conversational case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2 and analyses in Appendices 7–9.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same hierarchical parameter separation, semantic alignment channel, three parallel heads, and training objective. Appendix 10's DAG-PP inference procedure is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic dialogue coverage, LlamaQ, WebQ, TriviaQA, FDBench, FullDuplexBench 1.0/1.5, speech-quality evaluation, and conversational case scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2, Figure 4, and the supplementary analyses are unchanged. MOSS-Speech is newly discussed as related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The training and evaluation settings remain identical, including the 24 shared layers, 4/4/2-layer heads, one training epoch, batch size 32, greedy decoding, and benchmark metrics and procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablations, layer-depth study, Moshi gradient analysis, global gradient influence analysis, interruption/backchannel case study, and side-talk error analysis without revisions.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 reports evaluation with three random seeds and average performance in both versions. Run-count disclosure and uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Lychee-FD's Table 1 average speech-to-text/speech-to-speech accuracies remain 51.5/46.2, and Table 2's FullDuplexBench 1.5 IRR/BRR remain 78.0/69.0. The appendix results are identical.

T1.justification: The gradient definitions, cosine similarity and magnitude ratio, model and loss formulations, and Appendix 9's normalized influence score are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, gradient-conflict, knowledge-retention, and efficiency claims, including the reported 7.4% Spoken QA and 28.5% FullDuplexBench 1.5 improvements.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving gradient conflict, semantic dilution, knowledge retention, and latency are retained. The side-talk limitation and its attribution to insufficient multi-speaker intent coverage also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The embedded front-page Hugging Face hyperlink changes from HIT-TMG/Lychee-FD-1.5 to HIT-TMG/Lychee-FD, matching its existing displayed URL. Hardware, hyperparameters, code links, inference details, and data-generation instructions are otherwise unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in available weights.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds a focused discussion of MOSS-Speech's layer-wise speech–text analysis and modality-specific upper branches as complementary prior work. The bibliography is unchanged, and the accompanying Gao et al. (2025) entry is titled LUCY, leaving this new attribution unclear.

P1.justification: V4 makes a short related-work expansion, explicitly names Step-Audio, swaps the order of Yunxin Li and Xuanyu Zhang, and adds Tencent affiliation information. The remaining prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from PDF page 6 within the method discussion to page 7 within the experiments section. Added front matter and related-work text shift main-text page breaks. Scientific graphics, table formats, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added architectural context, better placement of Table 1, and agreement between the model hyperlink and displayed URL offer limited benefits. However, the new MOSS-Speech discussion cites an unchanged bibliography entry titled LUCY. The supplied PDFs do not resolve this attribution ambiguity, leaving the accuracy of the principal substantive addition uncertain and preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
